title: Z‑score anomaly detector for region health + soft fallback to quantized model variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Current region selection uses percentile thresholds (p50/p95) and simple additive network penalties. During transient network incidents we observe oscillation (flapping) and expensive hard-failovers that increase cost and violate latency SLOs. Goal: build a telemetry-driven region health gating mechanism using statistical anomaly detection (rolling z‑score on latency percentiles and packet-loss/err-rate) to compute a bounded Network Health Score (0-100) per region, apply smoothing/hysteresis, and enable a soft fallback path that preferentially routes to quantized/size-reduced model variants before performing costly cross-region failover.

Proposed approach:
1) Signals: ingest p50 and p95 latency distributions (per model variant), EWMA packet loss/5xx rate, and inter-pop RTT variance. Compute rolling-window mean and stddev (configurable window: default 5m, step 30s). Convert each signal to a z‑score and clamp to a capped range to avoid domination by a single metric.
2) Network Health Score (NHS): blend z‑scores with tuned weights into a 0..100 score where higher is healthier. Default weights: p95(0.45), p50(0.15), packet_loss(0.25), RTT_variance(0.15). Score mapping uses sigmoid mapping to reduce sensitivity to outliers.
3) Hysteresis & Smoothing: apply asymmetric hysteresis windows for demotion vs promotion: require 3 consecutive evaluation ticks (30s) below demotion threshold to mark a region degraded; require 6 consecutive ticks above promotion threshold to mark healthy. Also keep a cooldown timer (default 10m) after demotion to avoid flapping.
4) Soft Fallbacks: when NHS drops into the degraded band (50..65) we implement a progressive path: a) route 20% of new requests to local quantized model variant (Q8/Q4 depending on workload), b) enable local KV-prefix caching reuse for quantized variant to preserve quality, c) if NHS continues to fall (<50) escalate to tiered cross-region routing per policy. Soft fallback intended to preserve latency and reduce cross-pop egress.
5) Policy API: expose new routing policy object with fields: health_window, demote_threshold, promote_threshold, demote_count, promote_count, cooldown, quantized_variant_priority, soft_fallback_fraction, max_cross_region_reroute. Backwards-compatible defaults set for hosted and dedicated tiers.
6) Rollout plan: code gated behind feature-flag routing/zscore-health. Start with passive evaluation (score calc only) for 48h on canary POPs, then enable 5% soft fallback on low-traffic customers, monitor quality regressions.

Design doc & artifacts: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RT/ENG-21678+-+Zscore+Region+Health (design sketch, weight tuning notes, synthetic test harness), PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7482, dashboard mock: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/health/region-nhs

Metrics & success criteria:
- No increase in cross-region egress for affected customers during incidents (target: <5% delta)
- 95th token latency SLO adherence improves by >= 10% during degraded window vs baseline hard-failover
- Quality regression (evaluated via unit prompt set sampled traffic) < 2% delta in semantic similarity for quantized fallbacks

Test plan: unit tests for zscore computation, integration test with synthetic latency injector, staged canary with shadow traffic, A/B evaluation using redwood-evals for prompt quality on quantized variants.

Operational: add per-region NHS time-series with alerting (NHS<45 sustained 3m) to Console, add per-customer impact view showing soft fallback rates and quality regressions, and traceable request tags for fallback-path determination.

Risks & mitigations:
- Incorrect weight tuning causing over-demotion: mitigate by passive observation period and safe defaults.
- Quality regressions when swapping to quantized variant: mitigate via conservative initial soft fallback fraction (20%) and continuous quality evals, auto-rollback on regression alerts.
- Exploitable oscillation across many customers: mitigate using global coordination (central policy governor) and per-region cooldowns.

Next steps: finalize API shape, merge zscore calculator into telemetry pipeline, add policy config to routing service, implement soft fallback mixing and end‑to‑end canary test.
